subject: Ember AI — hosted per-token commit proposal & competitive comparison
messages:
From: Rachel Chen <rachel.chen@ember.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@ember.ai>, Derek Collins <derek.collins@ember.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing + commits — where Redwood lands vs Anthropic/OpenAI

Dylan —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We ran a short model-cost baseline and Ember's finance team asked me to get concrete on two things before we take a deeper eval:

1) What committed volume breakpoints do you support for the hosted API (per-token billing)? We currently have predictable monthly usage patterns and want to understand price steps.
2) If we commit, how does Redwood's effective per-token unit price compare to what we're paying now with Anthropic and our cloud provider managed endpoints?

A few context points: our current vendor mix is ~60% Anthropic chat for assisted writing and ~40% cloud-managed VMs for embeddings and generation. We're evaluating a 12–24 month commit. Cost parity with Anthropic in aggregate is the ask from procurement — they also want a short SLA addendum for latency and incident response.

Can you send a starter proposal and any comparables you have? If you can show a sample 12-month commit with blended per-token math that would help move this to our procurement review.

Best,
Rachel Chen
Head of ML Ops
Ember AI

---
Attachment: usage_snapshot_q1.csv (csv)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Chen <rachel.chen@ember.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@ember.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing + commits — where Redwood lands vs Anthropic/OpenAI

Rachel — thanks for the context and the usage snapshot. Appreciate the clear ask. High level answer up-front: we can build a 12- or 24-month commit that meets or beats your current blended per-token spend with Anthropic for chat + cloud-managed generation, while also giving you tooling advantages (prefetching, KV caching) that lower unit cost on bursty workloads.

I've attached an initial proposal (redwood_proposal_ember_q1.xlsx) with two commit structures:
- Bronze: 100M tokens/month guaranteed (12-month) — blended rate: $0.0009 / token for generation, $0.00045 / token for embeddings (example).
- Silver: 250M tokens/month guaranteed (12-month) — blended generation: $0.00065 / token; embeddings: $0.00035 / token.
- Gold: 500M tokens/month (12-month or 24-month options) — generation: $0.00042 / token; embeddings: $0.00028 / token.

Notes: these figures are illustrative in the sheet and include a 10% engineering-ops credit for migration and 60 days of prefunding credits to smooth transition. For customers comparing to Anthropic we typically show an apples-to-apples run at their typical prompt+tokens/session distribution — see Tab 'Comparative math' in the sheet.

Regarding SLA addendum: we can include a Targeted Latency SLO (p95 < 250 ms for 16k contexts on dedicated capacity) and a 4-hour P1 response commitment in a short SLA addendum; attaching a draft SLA_addendum_v1.pdf for procurement to review.

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm which commit tier you want to model (Bronze/Silver/Gold), 2) tell me if you need a 24-month vs 12-month illustration, and 3) identify any minimum legal terms (e.g., data residency, KMS). Once we have that, I can loop in Contracts and get a draft term sheet + DocuSign link.

Quick question: do you have a target blended per-token number (post-discounts) that procurement is aiming for? If so, we'll model against that explicitly.

Thanks — attaching the two files.

Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

---
Attachments: redwood_proposal_ember_q1.xlsx (xlsx), SLA_addendum_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing + commits — Ember quick ask (need approval on Silver tweak)

Laura / Vivek —

Looping you both in on Ember (Rachel Chen). They're mid-market, heavy Anthropic usage today, looking at a 12–24 month commit. I shared Bronze/Silver/Gold. Procurement asked for a targeted blended per-token that matches Anthropic's costs — they didn't share the exact number.

Ask: can we approve a limited Silver tweak: for a 12-month Silver (250M tokens/mo) give a temporary first-year blended rate of $0.00058 / generation token (down from $0.00065) if they sign by Apr 15 and do payment net 30 with a 6% prepay credit? This is a promotional concession but keeps headline economics favorable vs Anthropic (we still protect margin via committed throughput).

Risks: margin compression in Q2, but high probability of expansion to Gold in Q4 given their ingestion roadmap. Also procurement will want the SLA_addendum and DocuSign.

If you agree, I'll send a revised term sheet to Rachel and include a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Dylan

Rachel — quick follow-up with the revised Silver offer as discussed internally. Summary below; full math in the attached spreadsheet.

Revised Silver (12-month) — promotional first-year pricing if signed by Apr 15: 
- Commitment: 250M tokens / month guaranteed
- Effective generation rate (first 12 months): $0.00058 / token
- Effective embeddings rate (first 12 months): $0.00033 / token
- On-demand overage: $0.00095 / generation token (no change)
- Migration credit: 6% prepay credit if finance prepays at signing; also 60 days of usage credits to offset cutover
- SLA: include SLA_addendum_v1 (p95 latency target + 4h P1 response)

Competitive note: based on the usage profile you shared, this structure produces a blended monthly cost ~12% below your current Anthropic + cloud-managed mix (we modeled the same prompt sizes and embedding volume). The full comparative table and assumptions are in the spreadsheet (Tab: Comparative math).

If that works for Ember, reply with authorized signer name and procurement billing contact and I will generate the term sheet + DocuSign. We can also fast-track Dedicated capacity if you want stronger latency SLOs — we can include that as an option on the term sheet.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the transparent comparative math. Ember is happy to move forward on the revised Silver 12-month as long as a few items are included in the term sheet:

1) First-year promotional pricing as listed ($0.00058 gen / $0.00033 embed) with clear ramp clauses for year 2.
2) SLA addendum with an explicit credit schedule for p95 violations (we're proposing 10% credit for outages exceeding 4 hours).
3) Data residency confirmation: logs and customer data to remain in us-west region and KMS control retained by Ember.

If you can include those three items and send a DocuSign link by EOD Mon (Mar 29), we'll route to our legal and sign. Authorized signer is Derek Collins, CFO.
